chunks: But for him who lived in awe of the sublimity of his Lord, there will be two gardens --
ai.seo_question: What is the reward for those who fear the standing before their Lord?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, the 'two gardens' are often interpreted not merely as physical rewards but as symbolic representations of the dual spiritual stations of the Prophets and the Imams, or the two realms of this world and the hereafter. This verse underscores the centrality of *Taqwa* (God-consciousness) as the primary criterion for divine favor, linking the fear of standing before God directly to the attainment of eternal bliss.
